raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

I'm 54, been working this land 25 years. Only my wife and me at home now — the kids are grown and working in town, they send some money back. So labor is my biggest headache. 72 mu is a lot of land for two pairs of hands, and cotton especially... you can't pick 60 mu of cotton with two people. I've been doing this long enough to know what works.

**Cotton (about 60 mu):** This is my main crop. I've been growing cotton here for years — the land suits it, and there's a buyer in town who takes it every year. I plant around April 20th, maybe a few days earlier if the soil warms up, using plastic mulch like everyone does around here. Without mulch the ground's too cold and the seedlings don't come up right. I buy hybrid seed from the agri-store in the township — the same variety my cousin uses, he's had good luck with it, gets around 260-280 jin of lint per mu most years.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before planting — one bag of 15-15-15 per mu, that's about 50 jin, and then I top-dress with urea at budding time, maybe 20-25 jin per mu. Some of the younger guys apply more but I don't see the point — past a certain amount the plants just grow leaves and the bolls don't get better. I learned that the hard way about ten years ago when I put too much on and the plants got too tall and fell over.

Pesticide I have to use, no way around it. Bollworm, aphids, sometimes spider mites if it's dry. I spray maybe 4-5 times through the season. I ask the shop owner what's good this year — he sees what everyone else is buying.

Irrigation: I have a well, but pumping costs money — the diesel and the wear on the pump. I irrigate once before planting to get the ground soft, then once at flowering if it hasn't rained. That's usually enough. Some years I do a third time in July if it's really dry.

The big cost is picking. I hire workers from the village in September and October — usually 4-5 people for a few weeks. Pays about 1.5-2 yuan per jin picked. It adds up but I can't do it myself.

**Sunflower (about 12 mu):** I started putting sunflower on my worst piece of land — the one near the drainage ditch that doesn't grow cotton well. It's less work, doesn't need much fertilizer, and you can sell the seeds. I plant in late May after the ground is warm, use oil sunflower seed from the agri-store, maybe one compound fertilizer application at planting and that's it. One irrigation if it's dry at flowering. Birds are a problem at harvest — I just accept losing some. Yield maybe 300 jin per mu in a normal year.

I'm not trying to make a fortune — I just want a steady year. If cotton price drops I still have some sunflower and my wife's off-farm work. That's how I think about it.
